classification.difficultyReason: Uses reverse bearings to establish the specified included angle, applies the cosine rule for the direct distance, then chooses the correct orientation when converting a triangle angle into the return bearing.

content.prompt: Nathan leaves island $A$ in a boat and sails $152$ km on a bearing of $72^\circ$ to island $B$. Nathan then sails on a bearing of $196^\circ$ for $240$ km to island $C$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram in your book displaying all the information above.

answer.short: Diagram showing $AB=152$ km on bearing $072^\circ$ and $BC=240$ km on bearing $196^\circ$, with north references at $A$ and $B$.
answer.worked: Place $B$ northeast of $A$, then $C$ south and slightly west of $B$. Mark the clockwise bearings at $A$ and $B$, and label both distances.

spec.description: Two journey legs with north arrows at the bearing origins. House-style black marks replace decorative source shades.
spec.mathematics: AB has bearing 72° and length 152 km; BC has bearing 196° and length 240 km. Coordinates use one drawing unit per 60 km.

answer.worked:
The reverse bearing from $B$ to $A$ is $72^\circ+180^\circ=252^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=252^\circ-196^\circ\\\angle ABC&=56^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the distance from island $C$ to island $A$ is approximately $200$ km.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}CA^2&=152^2+240^2-2(152)(240)\cos56^\circ\\CA&=\sqrt{152^2+240^2-2(152)(240)\cos56^\circ}\\CA&\approx199.76\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

Thus the distance is approximately $200$ km.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Nathan wants to sail from island $C$ directly to island $A$. On what bearing should he sail? Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let $d=CA$, retaining the exact expression from part (c), and let $\theta=\angle BCA$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{240^2+d^2-152^2}{2(240)d}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{240^2+d^2-152^2}{480d}\right)\\\theta&\approx39.11^\circ\end{align*}$$

The reverse bearing from $C$ to $B$ is $196^\circ-180^\circ=016^\circ$. Since $CA$ lies west of $CB$,

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&=360^\circ+16^\circ-\theta\\\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&\approx336.89^\circ\end{align*}$$

Nathan should sail on a bearing of $337^\circ$.
